one_line_en: Jerusalem falls to Nebuchadnezzar; the Temple is burned.
Confucius is not yet born; Lu is ruled by Duke Cheng (r. 590–573; 586 is his fifth year); the Zhou king is a figurehead.
Solon's laws are eight years old; Athens is drifting toward the tyranny of Peisistratus.
Persia is still a vassal of the Medes; Cyrus is a child or not yet born.
Late Vedic ritual culture; the Buddha is not yet born on the short chronology.
Cyrus enters Babylon without a battle.
The exiles hear Second Isaiah name Cyrus as the LORD's anointed.
Confucius is about twelve years old in Lu.
The Ionian cities have been under Persian rule for some years: Harpagus subdued the mainland Ionians after the fall of Sardis.
Confucius, about fifty, serves briefly in the government of Lu.
The Buddha teaches in Magadha and Kosala (short chronology).
Yehud is a small Persian province; the Second Temple is fifteen years old.
Cleisthenes's democracy is eight years old; Heraclitus writes at Ephesus; the Ionian revolt is about to begin.
Darius rules from Susa and Persepolis over the largest empire yet seen.
Confucius dies in Lu.
The Greeks defeat the Persians at Plataea and Mycale; the Persian Wars end.
Xerxes withdraws from Greece.
Socrates is executed in Athens.
The Warring States era: Mozi's school is active; Mencius not yet born.
Within the range of the Buddha's death (short chronology).
On the short chronology the Buddha is not yet born; the oldest Upanishads are already behind the Ganges plain.
Yehud is a small Persian province and the Second Temple is about thirty-seven years old; no Hebrew text in this corpus is dated to this year.
On the short chronology the Buddha is somewhere between unborn and about twenty; the sources will not say which.
Yehud is a Persian province; the missions of Ezra and Nehemiah are dated by the regnal years of an Artaxerxes the books never identify, and may be just past or still to come.
The Achaemenid empire continues; Darius's inscription at Behistun is more than a century old.
Sardis falls to Cyrus and the Ionian cities pass under Persian rule; Thales's Miletus is now a subject city.
Cyrus takes Lydia and Persia reaches the Aegean.
Confucius is about five years old in Lu.
The Judeans are fifty years into the exile; Babylon is ruled by Nabonidus, who spends these years at Tayma in Arabia.
On the short chronology the Buddha is not yet born.
Zichan casts the penal code of Zheng in bronze, and Shuxiang writes from Jin to tell him he has ruined the state.
The first returnees are back in Jerusalem; the altar stands again and the foundation of the Temple is being laid.
Cyrus rules from Babylon to the Aegean.
The Ionian cities have been Persian subjects for a decade.
On the short chronology the Buddha is not yet born.
The Athenians beat the Persians at Marathon; Aeschylus is in the battle, thirty-five years old.
Darius's expedition against Eretria and Athens ends on the plain at Marathon.
Confucius is in his sixties, in the middle of his years of wandering between the states.
Yehud is a Persian province; the Second Temple is about twenty-five years old.
On the short chronology the Buddha is a child or a young man.
Thermopylae and Salamis: the Persian fleet is broken in the strait off Salamis.
Xerxes bridges the Hellespont, cuts a canal through Athos, and invades Greece.
Confucius is about seventy and has returned to Lu.
Yehud is a small Persian province, a generation after the Temple was finished.
On the short chronology the Buddha is a young man; nothing in the Indian record is dated to this year.
The Peloponnesian War breaks out, and Thucydides begins writing at the moment it does.
Confucius has been dead nearly fifty years and his disciples' schools are scattered among the states.
Artaxerxes I still reigns; he will die in the seventh winter of the Greek war.
Yehud under Persian rule; the Hebrew books that cover this period date themselves only by unidentified regnal years.
Within the Buddha's teaching life on the short chronology.
Athens surrenders, the long walls come down, and the Thirty are installed.
The Warring States: Mozi's school is active and the Mohist canon is being assembled.
Yehud under Persian rule, between the Temple's completion and whatever date is right for Ezra.
Within the range of the Buddha's death on the short chronology.
Darius II has died; Artaxerxes II is king, and his brother Cyrus, accused of plotting, has been arrested and sent back to his province.
